requirement: `habeas status` and the mdBook requirements index MUST generate their Definition/Evidence Markdown tables through the same renderer. That renderer MUST calculate column widths, align the columns, and display the same evidence-state labels in both outputs. Callers MAY select different definitions and supply different kind-labeled name cells so mdBook can link to detail pages.
rationale:
`requirements.cli.shared_status_rendering` is satisfied. Both outputs go through one renderer, and tests cover alignment and the evidence-state labels in each.

**Same renderer.**
- `src/commands.rs#fn[status_markdown_with_github]` builds its rows and calls `render_evidence_table`.
- `src/commands.rs#fn[status_markdown_with_options]`, which carries the `{impl}`, calls it, so it is reachable.
- `src/index.rs#impl[DetailPlan]/fn[populate]` builds its rows and calls the same function.
- That function is `src/markdown.rs#fn[render_evidence_table]`.

**Column widths and alignment.** `render_evidence_table` takes the maximum cell length per column, with the header text as the minimum. It pads every row, including the `---` separator row, to that width. Both tests assert this. They check that pipe positions match on every line and that each column's width equals its widest trimmed cell.
- CLI: `tests/commands.rs#fn[status_tables_align_each_column_to_its_widest_cell]`, run with and without `--all`.
- Index: `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]`.

**Same evidence-state labels.** Both callers pass `evidence.state().label()`, taken from `LoadedDetailEvidence` and `EvidenceState`. The CLI test checks the Valid, Missing, Determination false and Invalid labels. The index test checks the same labels in the mdBook table.

**Callers MAY select different definitions and name cells.** This is a MAY, so nothing needs checking. It is also implemented as stated: the status code filters by glob and `--all` and uses plain `` `name` (kind)`` cells, while the index uses linked `[`name`](href) (kind)` cells.

I found no unspecified behavior and no untested obligation. Only the `{impl}` and `{test}` references named in the inputs are involved.
